Figure 3. Comparison of penalized graphon Hawkes estimates for the Allen Neuropixels session 715093703, based on spike events in the time interval [5000, 5250]. Panels (A)–(B) display the estimated baseline intensity and graphon using a spatial basis of Legendre polynomials, whereas panels (C)–(D) use a spatial basis of Haar wavelets. All quantities are normalized by the empirical frequency 𝑓 . The estimator based on Legendre polynomials produces smoother and more spatially regular estimates, while the results in panels (C)–(D) appear as discretized variants of those in panels (A)–(B).

Figure 4. Non-penalized least-squares estimates for the Allen Neuropixels session 715093703, based on spike events in the interval [5000, 5250], are shown in Panels (A)–(B), where a spatial basis of Haar wavelets is used with 𝜂 = 0. All quantities are normalized by the empirical frequency 𝑓 . In contrast to the penalized estimates in Figure 3(C)–(D), the non-penalized solution exhibits pronounced spatial irregularity, with large oscillations and substantial negative values of the graphon over parts of the domain. These findings indicate that, while the unregularized estimator can capture fine-scale variation, it is highly sensitive to sampling noise and produces estimates that are difficult to interpret in terms of underlying connectivity structure.
